The Police Sub-Inspector of R.T. Nagara Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused for the offence punishable under Section 498(A), 506 of Indian Penal Code.
2. Prosecution Case:
The marriage of CW1 Smt. Anitha.V and accused was solemnized on 21/09/2018.

After the marriage, they were residing at No.13, ground floor, 5th Cross, 3rd Main, L.
D. Block within the limits of R. T. Nagara Police Station.
At KABC030159642020 CC No.4212/2020 that time, the accused started ill-treating CW1 even for trivial issues.
The accused made CW1 to walk for 6 to 7 kilometers during her pregnancy and on account of which, pregnancy was ended in miscarriage thereby subjected her to mental and physical cruelty.
On 30-12-2019, the accused abused CW1 with filthiest language and threatened her with dire consequences.

3. First Information Report: On the basis of first information given by informant cum CW1 namely Smt. Anitha, the HC of R.T.Nagara police station Sri Theerthappa, registered Crime No.287/2019 against the accused for the offence punishable under Section 498(A), 506 IPC, prepared FIR and sent the same to the Court and to his superior officers.
4. Investigation:

After registration of case, CW10 namely Smt.Premakumari PSI of R.T. Nagara PS,
drawn spot mahazar as per Ex.P2 on 31-12-2019, recorded the requisite witnesses and collected the documents and submitted the charge sheet against accused for the offences punishable under Sec.498A, 506 of IPC.
5.
On receipt of charge sheet, this Court took cognizance of offence alleged against the accused.
The accused was enlarged on bail by the order dated 11-02-2022.
7. Copies of prosecution papers as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused.

8. Charge: After hearing learned Sr.APP and counsel for accused, charge for the offences punishable U/Sec.498(A), 504, 506 of Indian Penal Code, has been framed, read over and explained to the accused in the language known to him, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
9. Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 10 witnesses and examined 1 witness and exhibited 2 documents.

The learned Senior APP prayed for issuance of summons to other witnesses however his prayer was rejected on the ground that no purpose would be served as PW1 and the accused has compromised the matrimonial differences amongst them in M C No.7469/2024 and hence the examination of CW2 to CW10 was dispensed with by the order dated 31/01/2025.

Anitha V vs Mani Prasad on 1 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26607805/
2 KABC030159642020 CC No.4212/2020 10.

Accused statement as per section 313 of CrPC: After completion of evidence of prosecution, the accused was examined as per section 313 statement of Cr.P.C, wherein he denied incriminating evidence appearing in the statement of PW1 and did not lead any rebuttal evidence.
11.
Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

12. The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
1.
Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that after the marriage, the accused started ill-treating CW1 even for trivial issues.

The accused made CW1 to walk for 6 to 7 kilometers during her pregnancy and on account of which, pregnancy was ended in abortion thereby subjected her to mental and physical cruelty thereby resulted in commission of the offence punishable under Sec.498(A) of IPC?

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on 30-12-2019 at No.13,
ground floor, 5th Cross, 3rd Main, L.D. Block within the limits of R.T.Nagara Police Station the accused abused CW1 with filthiest language knowingly such abusive words will provoke breach of peace thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec. 504 of IPC?
3.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said date and place, the accused threatened CW1 with dire consequences thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.506 of IPC?
4. What order?

The findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1-3 : In the Negative Point No.4 : As per final order REASONS 14. Point No.1 to 3: These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution has examined one witness, which is as follows:
i. CW1 by name Smt. Anitha.V, being Informant examined as PW1 deposed that her marriage with the accused took place on 21/9/2018, and after marriage, while she was living in Ganganagar, Bengaluru, the accused was working as a Guest Lecturer.
After a month of marriage, the accused picked up quarrel with her and ill-treated her.

Anitha V vs Mani Prasad on 1 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26607805/
3
When she was pregnant, accused used to take her to his hometown and also an exhibition program held at GKVK College by walking about 6-7 k.m.
KABC030159642020 CC No.4212/2020 which led to miscarriage.

On 30-12-2019,
the accused started to quarrel with with her, beaten her with a stick, abused her and threatened her, unable to bear his harassment, she filed a complaint as per Ex.P1,
police conducted spot mahazar as per Ex.P2.
15.
In this case, PW1 is the informant cum victim, initially supported the case of prosecution, but in her further chief examination deposed that:
She denied the further statement given before police as per Ex.P3.

On perusal of the above recital, it is appear that the disputes between the accused and CW1(informant) in M.C.No.7469/2024 have been settled and she had received gold ornaments and Rs.10 lakhs and Rs.1 lakh from accused as alimony/settlement amount.

16. This court places reliance in the case of B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. State of haryana and anr in the case of AIR 2003 SCW 1824, wherein it was held that, "in a case where matrimonial disputes have been resolved between the parties then in that case offence under Section 498A of I.P.C. may be compounded between the parties for according to them an opportunity to settle in life afresh.

entities.text: B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. State of haryana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
and in the case of Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C.
KABC030159642020 CC No.4212/2020 808 (Pat), wherein this lordship observed which runs thus:
"It appears that good sense have been prevailed amongst the spouses and when it became impossible for them to lead conjugal life any further and when the matrimonial home has been broken for all practical purposes, they have decided to withdraw all allegations and counter allegations against each other and get themselves separated on divorce by mutual consent.

entities.text:
Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C.
KABC030159642020 CC No.4212/2020 808 (Pat)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although, Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code is not compoundable, but in the nature and circumstances of the case and the situation prevailing, accord is hereby granted to compromise the dispute between the parties and hence joint petition filed in both the cases are hereby allowed."

Anitha V vs Mani Prasad on 1 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26607805/
4

It further held that after examining the nature of the case and the circumstances, under which the offence has been committed, it would be proper to compound the offence and in my opinion, it would be also meet the ends of justice."
ADMITTEDLY, the disputes between the PW1 and accused No.1 have been resolved.
The criminal KABC030159642020 CC No.4212/2020 case under Section 498A of I.P.C. is the off-shoot of the said matrimonial dispute.
The parties have come to their terms and in pursuance thereto the CW1/PW1 does not intend to proceed with this case and hence she has not supported the prosecution case.

17. In the case of the KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464,
wherein it was held that "it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end".

entities.text: KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18. Under these circumstances and on account of the preposition laid down by the Hon'ble Apex and Hon'ble High Court, even if other witnesses examined by the prosecution, they did supported the prosecution, would not helpful to the prosecution.
Under these circumstances, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of the Court in examining other witnesses.
Moreover the evidence of other KABC030159642020 CC No.4212/2020 witnesses is only formal in nature.

Therefore, the prayer of learned Sr.APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed and hence the ingredients for offence under section 498A of IPC with other offences under section 504, 506 of IPC was not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, this court answer the point No.1 to 3 in the Negative.

19. Point No.4:- In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused is found not guilty and acquitted from the offence punishable under Sec.498(A), 504, 506 of Indian Penal Code.
(ii) Accused is set at liberty.

(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C his bail bond shall be in force for 6 (six)
months.
KABC030159642020 CC No.4212/2020 (iv) Ordered accordingly.

(Deepa.V.),
